title: Production Stabilization — Fix CRITICAL Issues from Code Review
decision: Execute a dedicated stabilization sprint (SPRINT-NF-STAB-001) addressing all CRITICAL and HIGH severity findings from the 2026-08-20 code review. Work is organized into three sequential phases: Phase 1 (Security & Stability), Phase 2 (Data Integrity), Phase 3 (Architecture Compliance). No new features accepted during this sprint.
rationale:
Code review identified 14 CRITICAL issues blocking production deployment:

1. Secrets (.env, keys) sent to LLM without redaction — direct credential leak (arch ch.46)
2. Event store is in-memory — complete event loss on Node restart (arch ch.43)
3. Dead-letter queue never drains — unbounded memory growth
4. Subscription handler crash kills entire event pipeline (single point of failure)
5. History archive is in-memory — archived records lost on restart
6. Persistent event store has DB-vs-memory inconsistency race
7. Concurrent workflow transitions silently overwrite state
8. Context budget is advisory only — token firewall broken (arch ch.49)
9. Test runner has no timeout — hangs indefinitely (arch ch.44)
10. Idempotency cache has race condition under error paths (arch ch.42)
11. Database writes have no transaction wrapping — partial writes possible
12. database.close() crashes on startup failure
13. project_id lost during event persistence — breaks multi-project
14. Replay engine covers <10% of event types

Architecture compliance is ~73%. These issues represent data loss, security vulnerability, and reliability risks that must be resolved before any feature work continues.
alternatives: Defer all fixes — ship current code and patch reactively as bugs surface. Risk: unrecoverable data loss, credential leaks, cascading failures under load.
Fix everything in one sprint — too many interdependent changes creates high merge conflict risk and makes individual verification difficult.
Phase by module instead of severity — slower time-to-security-fix exposes credentials longer, harder to measure aggregate progress.
consequences: Positive: Eliminates credential leak vector via secrets redaction. All stores survive Node restarts. Error isolation prevents single-handler failures from taking down the system. Architecture compliance rises above 95%.
Negative: Blocks all new feature development for the duration of the stabilization sprint (~15–20 engineering days). Introduces migration complexity for existing event and history tables.
Trade-off: Team capacity is fully consumed by stability work. Short-term velocity drops to zero for features.
Long-term: Establishes foundation for reliable multi-project operation, advanced memory features, and dashboard UI work.
